title: Why Growth Often Begins When We Become Quiet
headline: How to Hear God: Why Growth Begins With Listening
headline_sub: Speak, Lord, Your Servant Is Listening
tagline: Many people want God’s guidance. Few create space for His voice.
seo_title: How to Hear God's Voice: Why Growth Begins With Listening | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Maybe hearing God isn't difficult; listening is. A devotional for men on James 1:19, 1 Samuel 3:10 and Elijah's gentle whisper.
verse_text: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry.

scriptures.text: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry.
Speak, Lord, for Your servant is listening.
I am the way, and the truth, and the life….

items: Most people think communication is about speaking.
Scripture often presents wisdom as listening.
Many men spend their lives:
reacting,
explaining,
defending,
teaching,
fixing,
advising.
Few learn how to truly listen.

blocks.text: Because listening requires something many men struggle with:

items: The loudest voice in your life often becomes the most influential.
The question is: have you left enough room for God to speak?
Most men live in a constant stream of noise.
Podcasts. News. Social media. Notifications. Meetings. Opinions. Entertainment.
And beneath all of that noise is a deeper problem.
Many men are uncomfortable with silence.
Silence exposes anxiety, distractions, unresolved thoughts and hidden fears.
So we keep filling space.
But Scripture repeatedly shows that God often speaks differently than we expect.
Not through volume.
Through attentiveness.
Many believers think hearing God is difficult.
The reality may be: listening is difficult.
Think about Elijah.
God wasn’t in the wind, the earthquake or the fire.
God came through a gentle whisper.
The issue wasn’t God’s ability to speak.
The issue was Elijah’s ability to listen.
Notice the order in James 1:19.
Listening first.
Speaking second.
Modern culture reverses this.
We are quick to speak, quick to react, quick to post, quick to defend.
But wisdom slows down.
Wisdom listens.
Young Samuel responds, “Speak Lord, for Your servant is listening.”
He doesn’t say, “Listen Lord, because I have something important to tell You.”
His posture is receptivity.
Availability.
Surrender.
The more certain you are that you already know everything….
the less teachable you become.
The more teachable you become….
the more you begin hearing things you previously missed.
Surface thought: “I already know that.”
Possible root: pride, hurry, distraction, self-reliance.
Deeper question: Have I become more interested in speaking than listening?
Core lie: “I already know what I need.”
Truth: Humility keeps learning.
Greater truth: God often reveals more to the listening heart than the talking one.

blocks.text: A man who cannot listen cannot continue growing.
